born.why: The previous code treated any fruit with *any* harm record as bad, ignoring that some species are safe and others vary. This new code distinguishes between "never eaten safely" (risky, requires high hunger to taste) and "proven safe" (good to eat), allowing Fagi to exploit known food sources while remaining cautious of new ones until desperation forces a trial.

The code tracks cumulative harm vs. benefit per species to reliably identify poisonous fruits and avoid them, while prioritizing eating fully safe/beneficial fruits and cautiously tasting unknown ones only when hungry.

The code prioritizes safety by explicitly checking for known toxic traits before acting, distinguishes between proven food sources and uncertain ones by requiring a full portion history or safe sampling to commit to eating, and uses hunger thresholds to decide when to explore novel fruits versus relying on known safe foods.

The code improves survival by tracking both specific species and shared traits (color, smell, shape) to infer toxicity across related fruits, prioritizing tasting when starving and avoiding items with high harm-to-feed ratios.

The code prioritizes safety by tracking harm vs. feed counts per species; it avoids proven toxic fruits ('leave'), cautiously tests novel ones ('taste'), and exploits safe fruits by carrying them for later or eating immediately based on hunger levels, thereby balancing risk and survival.

The previous code treated any first-time encounter as risky if it wasn't immediately harmful, missing the nuance that unknown fruits are valuable data points; this version explicitly distinguishes between "unknown" (taste if safe margin exists), "known bad" (leave), and "known good" (eat/carry based on hunger and inventory state), allowing Fagi to learn from novel foods without unnecessary starvation risk.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding fruits with any history of harm (poison), while allowing trials on novel or unconfirmed fruits only when hunger is high enough to justify the risk, and efficiently consuming known safe fruits to maintain energy levels.
